prerequisites: Basic knowledge of linear algebra, differential and integral calculus, vectorial analysis, differential equations.
Basic concepts of electromagnetic fields and waves.

learning_outcomes.text: Manage the basic parameters and regulations on electromagnetic emissions of a radiating system.
Analyze the effects of reflection and transmission of electromagnetic waves and interpret their behavior.

Interpret the engineering parameters that define the elements of a radio link based on the application, and in particular, those of antennas, their value ranges and units, as well as their technical specifications (also in English).
Identify an antenna type, analyze its characteristics, frequency band, and applications.
Perform the balance of a link with basic propagation losses, interpret the propagation mechanisms associated with the environment and frequency bands, and use models to quantify them.
Analyze the specifications and parameters of the specific components of a satellite link.
Identify and compare different satellite transmission systems based on orbit, applications, and services offered by organizations and consortia.
Understand the technical and regulatory fundamentals of frequency allocation, and be able to handle national and international frequency attribution tables.

syllabus_topics: PARAMETERS OF ANTENNAS, TYPES OF ANTENNAS AND THEIR CHARACTERIZATION.
Engineering parameters for the characterization of transmitter and receiver antennas (matching parameters, gain functions, polarization, EIRP, radiation efficiency, illumination efficiency).
Other types of antennas in wireless communications.
FREE-SPACE RADIO LINK BUDGET. TERRESTRIAL PROPAGATION, CHARACTERIZATION AND MODELS.
Characterization and specifications of link elements.
Parameters related to signal-to-noise ratio, sensitivity, error probability, transmission speed and capacity, for the evaluation of reception in analog and digital radio links.
Design of a radio link with reflection and obstacles.
Effect of tropospheric refraction and rectilinear propagation equivalent.
Ionospheric propagation: description and balance of an ionospheric link.
Characteristics of multipath and mobile propagation; characterization parameters and operating criteria.
Empirical and numerical models for the characterization of propagation and the calculation of radio coverage.
Regulation on the use of the radio electric public domain and National Frequency Allocation Table (CNAF).
Environmental impact of electromagnetic emissions: regulation of human exposure to electromagnetic emissions.
COMMUNICATIONS SATELLITES. ORBITS. SYSTEMS AND APPLICATIONS. SATELLITE RADIO LINK.
Examples of orbits associated with different missions and services; comparisons.
Characterization of specific elements of the satellite link (on-board transponder, satellite antennas, transmitters, receivers and antennas in earth stations).
Link budget and specific loss factors.

Some examples of configuration and specifications of satellite transmission systems (TV-SAT, broadcasting, V-SAT, telephony, internet, location, navigation, security, earth observation and environmental applications).
Frequency bands, allocation to systems and services.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary examination, the final grade is calculated as (0.70 x T) + (0.3 x P), where T is the theoretical block grade and P is the practical block grade. A minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required in the theoretical block written exam. If this minimum is not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated formula result and 4.0. In the extraordinary examination, students can choose to use the practical block grade (P) from the ordinary examination with the same formula, provided they obtain a minimum of 4 out of 10 in the extraordinary written exam (T). Alternatively, students can opt for a single written exam for the entire course, whose grade will be the final grade.
